title: Sociocultural and economic influences on customers

match.reason: No existing point teaches how sociocultural and economic factors shape customer choices; the closest ones cover environmental influences on the business itself, which is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Sociocultural and economic influences
card: Sociocultural
Social and cultural groups shape what people buy. Family, friends and peers, social class and culture all affect what a customer sees as normal or wanted.
Examples
A teenager may buy a brand because friends use it. A family tradition or a cultural festival may lead a household to buy particular foods or clothes.
Economic
Income sets how much customers can spend. The state of the economy matters too: when jobs are scarce or interest rates are high, many households cut back on non-essential items.
A marketer studies both kinds of influence to decide who to target, what to offer and how to price it.
draft.remember: Who customers mix with and what they can afford both shape what they buy.

a.q: Which purchase is best explained by a sociocultural influence?
opts: Sam buys a skateboard brand because all his friends ride it
Ava buys a cheaper brand of rice after her pay is cut
Leo buys a phone because he likes how it feels to hold
Priya buys an umbrella because it started raining
a.why: Sam is following the choices of his friends, which is a peer influence and so sociocultural. Ava's choice is about a fall in income, which is an economic influence, so it is the tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Look for a choice shaped by other people.

b.q: Interest rates rise and many households in Tamworth have less money left after paying their home loans. Dev owns a restaurant there. Which change in customer behaviour is most likely?
opts: Fewer families dine out, so Dev may add cheaper meals
More families dine out, because friends often eat out
Families keep dining out, because of cultural habits
Families dine out less only if their friends do too
b.why: Higher loan repayments leave less income to spend, so households tend to cut back on non-essentials such as dining out. Friends and culture can influence choices, but here the change comes from the economy, so the sociocultural options do not fit.
b.clue: Ask what has changed: who customers mix with, or what they can afford?

a.best: Sam buys a skateboard brand because all his friends ride it

b.best: Fewer families dine out, so Dev may add cheaper meals

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'). One distractor uses the absolute 'only'. Together these cues let a test-wise student pick the answer without knowing the idea.
